boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Iowa, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A walkable, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence that starts with campus landmarks, builds in museums and study space, and finishes with low-key Iowa City exploration.

cards.title: Start with the Pentacrest
cards.subtitle: Campus orientation stop
cards.notes: Walk the lawn boundary from Clinton to Madison and Washington to Jefferson, then use Old Capitol at its center to get your bearings.
cards.short_summary: Begin with the campus landscape that frames Old Capitol and academic buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The university identifies the Pentacrest as the area bounded by Clinton, Washington, Madison, and Jefferson streets, with Old Capitol at its center.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; events and classes may be scheduled there.

cards.title: Step inside Old Capitol
cards.subtitle: 21 N. Clinton St.
cards.notes: Continue from the lawn into the museum and take a self-guided look at the galleries and history panels during public open hours.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus-building visit with a self-guided option.
cards.evidence_claim: Old Capitol Museum is open to the public with always-free admission, and visitors may take self-guided tours during open hours.
cards.source_title: Group Visits & Tours | Old Capitol Museum
cards.access_notes: Self-guided visits are available during open hours; groups of more than 10 should schedule ahead.

cards.entity_name: University of Iowa Museum of Natural History
cards.title: Browse Macbride Hall galleries
cards.subtitle: 11 Macbride Hall
cards.notes: Make this your next indoor stop and explore the Iowa, Bird, and Mammal halls at your own pace while the museum is open.
cards.short_summary: Natural-history galleries a short walk from Old Capitol.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Natural History is open to the public with always-free admission; its self-guided galleries include Iowa, Bird, and Mammal halls.
cards.source_title: Group Visits & Tours | University of Iowa Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: Public hours are Wednesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; confirm holiday exceptions before going.

cards.title: Pick a Main Library study spot
cards.subtitle: 125 W. Washington St.
cards.notes: Pause for a plan-your-week session: choose a quiet seat or meet up in a group-study area, then check the library’s current access details.
cards.short_summary: A flexible campus reset with quiet, group, and technology-enabled spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: University sources list quiet and group study spaces, computers, and an active learning area in the Main Library.
cards.access_notes: Listed public building hours include until 1 a.m. Monday–Thursday and Sunday; hours exclude holidays, breaks, and special events.

cards.title: See what is on at the Stanley
cards.subtitle: 160 W. Burlington St.
cards.notes: Walk south from the library, check the gallery plan, and give yourself time to look closely rather than trying to see every room.
cards.short_summary: A free art-museum stop beside the Main Library and Gibson Square Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The Stanley Museum of Art is adjacent to Gibson Square Park and the Main Library, and admission is always free.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit | Stanley Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Gallery hours vary by day; the museum states that admission ends five minutes before gallery closing.

cards.title: Use the IMU as your campus hub
cards.subtitle: 125 N. Madison St.
cards.notes: Stop at the Welcome Center or settle into a public study area, and check renovation updates before depending on a particular room or service.
cards.short_summary: A central student-life building with study spaces, services, and changing renovation conditions.
cards.evidence_claim: The university describes the IMU as centrally located and lists study spaces, Wi-Fi, computer labs, dining options, and the Learning Commons.
cards.access_notes: The IMU reports renovations in progress; verify building hours and the availability of specific spaces before arrival.

cards.title: Move at the CRWC
cards.subtitle: 309 S. Madison St.
cards.notes: If you have facility access, choose a low-pressure activity such as the track, pool, or open recreation; review entry and facility hours first.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation stop with fitness, pool, track, and court facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The CRWC includes fitness space, a climbing wall, pools, a jogging track, and basketball/volleyball courts.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation and Wellness Center | Recreational Services
cards.access_notes: Recreational Services lists paid daily walk-ins and membership access; check current hours and eligibility before visiting.

cards.title: Walk out to Hancher Green
cards.subtitle: Outside Hancher Auditorium, 141 Park Rd.
cards.notes: Use the riverside lawn as a breather between stops, then check Hancher’s current calendar for any all-ages outdoor program you may want to attend.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor performance-lawn destination beside Hancher Auditorium.
cards.evidence_claim: Hancher identifies Hancher Green as the outdoor location at Hancher Auditorium, 141 Park Road, and has hosted all-ages public events there.
cards.source_title: Hancher Green event information | Hancher Auditorium
cards.access_notes: Outdoor events and ticketing vary; consult Hancher’s current event listing before making plans.

cards.title: Cross downtown to the public library
cards.subtitle: 123 S. Linn St., downtown Iowa City
cards.notes: Settle in with a book, browse a floor, or use this as a calm meet-up point before your group heads back toward campus.
cards.short_summary: A downtown reading-and-regrouping stop with published daily hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Iowa City Public Library lists its downtown location at 123 South Linn Street and publishes hours every day of the week.
cards.source_title: Hours & Location | Iowa City Public Library
cards.access_notes: Published hours are Monday–Thursday 10 a.m.–9 p.m., Friday 10 a.m.–8 p.m., Saturday 10 a.m.–6 p.m., and Sunday noon–5 p.m.; special closures apply.

cards.title: End on the Literary Walk
cards.subtitle: Downtown Iowa City sidewalks
cards.notes: Finish by following the city’s Literary Walk map and pausing at bronze sidewalk panels; it is an easy way to notice the downtown on foot.
cards.short_summary: A self-paced public-art walk that connects downtown streets with Iowa City’s writing culture.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Iowa City lists an Iowa City Literary Walk Map within its public-art resources and describes bronze panels installed along Iowa Avenue.
cards.source_title: Your Public Art | City of Iowa City
cards.access_notes: Use the city’s Literary Walk map and stay on public sidewalks; allow extra time if stopping to read panels.
